_note: This file may carry comments; executor-policy.json may NOT (AWS rejects unknown keys). Read alongside docs/adr/0007-row-4-cannot-live-in-iam.md and docs/adr/0010-pin-updateservice-condition-keys.md.
_known_weakness: ecs:UpdateService is a single IAM action covering all three ActionTypes. IAM cannot distinguish them, and cannot bound desiredCount. Row 6's guarantee is therefore coarser than one-action-per-ActionType. Stated plainly rather than glossed.
_conditions: Pinned per ADR-0010 (Proposed). check_iam_scope.py requires every Allow statement granting the action to carry these exact operators and values. ecs:task-definition pins the family NAME, not its task role; it holds because the Executor cannot register revisions. Any revision in the family, including a known-bad one, stays reachable. IfExists behaviour is read from AWS docs, not observed; Sprint 5 confirms it with denied calls. The enable-execute-command pin conflicts with reaching chaos endpoints through ECS Exec, if that becomes the access path; that is undecided. The family name orders-api is assumed from the service name until Terraform defines it.
_not_yet_pinned: The other 11 UpdateService condition keys, and the reason each is unpinned, are listed in ADR-0010. UpdateService has no security-group condition key at all.
